usageRows.usage: Read & write repositories, including org repos

requirements.label: Each org's owners must approve your OAuth app before members can grant it access to org repos

usageRows.notes: Personal repos work immediately. Org repos need per-org owner approval, which is on by default for new orgs.

defaultUsageReason.text: Most GitHub agents read and write code, issues and PRs in org repos, which needs the repo scope.

verdict.oneLiner: Self-serve in about 30 minutes with no GitHub review. Org repos need each org's owners to approve your app.

preApprovalLimits.text: Until an org's owners approve your app, its members can't grant it access to that org's resources.

steps.title: Copy the Composio callback URL
steps.detail: In Composio: Authentication management → Create Auth Config → GitHub → OAuth2 → Use your own developer credentials. Copy the redirect URI it shows: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback (it stays on /api/v3/ even though Composio's REST API is v3.1). GitHub needs an exact match unless you enable wildcard matching.

steps.title: Register a new OAuth app on GitHub
steps.detail: Profile picture → Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps → New OAuth App. Fill in Application name (shown on the consent screen), Homepage URL and Authorization callback URL (paste the Composio URL). Register under an org account if the app belongs to your company.

blockers.workaround: Delete unused apps or register under an org

steps.title: Generate a client secret
steps.detail: On the app page, click Generate a new client secret and copy it immediately. GitHub shows it only once.
takeoverPoints: Sudo / 2FA prompt if your sign-in is older

steps.title: Paste the credentials into the Composio auth config
steps.detail: Paste the Client ID and Client secret into the auth config from step 1, then add the scopes you need (e.g. repo, read:org).

steps.title: Connect your own account and run one tool
steps.detail: Open the Connect Link, check the consent screen shows your app's name, then run one action (e.g. list repos).

steps.title: Get your app approved in users' orgs
steps.detail: When a user authorizes, they can request access for each org. The org's owners get a notification and approve it under Third-party access.

blockers.workaround: Personal repos still work. For org-wide installs, consider a GitHub App, which orgs install directly.

whileYouWait.text: Keep using Composio managed auth for GitHub while orgs approve your app.

gotchas.text: New OAuth apps default to expiring user tokens: access tokens last 8 hours and refresh tokens expire after 6 months unused.
The rate limit is 5,000 requests/hour per user, shared with that user's other apps and tokens.
OAuth app access restrictions are on by default for new orgs, so org repos stay invisible until an owner approves.
Switching from managed auth to your own OAuth app doesn't migrate existing connections: users reconnect, or you import their credentials where supported.

The consent screen says "Authorizing will redirect to https://backend.composio.dev", so users see Composio's domain even with your own app. To show yours, register a redirect on your domain that 302-forwards to Composio's callback.
A brand-new app shows "Created less than a day ago" and "Fewer than 10 GitHub users" on the consent screen. Own it from an org (not a personal account) so the consent screen names your company.

unknowns: No GitHub page states verbatim that OAuth apps need no review; the R0/R1 levels rest on the absence of any review step (Setup agent attempt pending).
